resources.string: This device does not report network counters.

To measure each app\u2019s data use, Mizan needs the Usage access permission from system settings. Android grants broader access than that (which apps you use), but Mizan reads byte counters only and never sends anything off the device.
Figures come from Android\u2019s counters as of the last sync and can trail the current moment by minutes.

Keep the apps you choose off the internet — locally, without root.
Android requires explicit consent before any app can create a VPN tunnel. The system dialog appears once; after that, Mizan can block traffic from the apps you block on your device.

When enabled, Android routes only the blocked apps into a local tunnel inside Mizan. Their packets never leave the device; they are dropped here. Every other app stays outside the tunnel and works normally.
Mizan has no internet permission, so it cannot send your data to any server. No analytics, no accounts, and every list and decision stays on your device.

One VPN at a time: enabling Mizan\u2019s guard disconnects any other VPN. A VPN icon appears in the status bar. Blocked apps are blocked on metered networks only (usually mobile); on unmetered Wi-Fi they work normally.
You can revoke consent from the system\u2019s VPN settings at any time.

How it works, and who we are
Everything happens inside your phone: no server, no account, and not a single figure leaves the device.

Mizan reads Android\'s own network counters: TrafficStats for the live rate, and NetworkStatsManager for daily and per-app usage. It neither estimates nor guesses; it shows what the system recorded, which is why the figures match your device settings.

When protection is on, Mizan creates a local VpnService tunnel on the device itself. Traffic passes through it to be decided: what you allowed goes through, and packets from blocked apps are dropped before they leave. The app opens no outside connection, needs no root, and does not hold the Internet permission at all.
Built from scratch: no servers, no middlemen, and your data never leaves your device.
Made to serve the individual and protect their privacy, with no commercial goals or tracking.
Stop background drain and fully control which apps may reach the network.
We are the Maknoon Team — young people from Al-Salam neighbourhood, building and engineering independent software and apps.
To build safe, free software from scratch, without relying on middlemen or external servers, serving and protecting the user\'s data.
Applies immediately to screens, notifications and widgets.
What every screen and figure means

Tap Start on the dashboard and the meter runs in the background. A persistent notification shows the live speed and today\'s total, with a pause action. While monitoring is stopped no new figures are recorded.

The speed card shows download and upload live. The today card shows usage since midnight, and \u201cpartial\u201d means the day was not fully monitored. The budget bar appears only when a cap exists. The status line says whether measurement is running, stopped, or unable to read the counters.

The ongoing notification is silent and refreshes every second; tapping it opens the app. Both widgets are optional: a 2\u00d71 speed widget and a 2\u00d72 budget ring, added from the launcher, each with its own settings. The status-bar badge shows the rate next to the clock in the template you pick.

The chart covers the last seven days (download over upload), and below it the 24 hours of today. A day without monitoring stays an empty column rather than a zero, and the amber dot marks a partial day. Export writes a CSV to Downloads through the system picker.

This screen needs Usage Access from system settings. The figures come from Android\'s counters and can lag a few minutes behind usage. Pick Today, 7 days, or the billing cycle; tap an app for its chart and its mobile/Wi-Fi split. System apps are not listed.

Set a daily or monthly cap for the device and for each app, in MB or GB; switching the unit only rewrites the number and never the cap (2 GB = 2000 MB). At 80% one \u201capproaching\u201d alert arrives, at 100% one \u201cexceeded\u201d alert, once per level per period, and it stays until you tap \u201cOK\u201d. The billing cycle starts on the day you choose, 1\u201328.

Protection blocks chosen apps from the network through a local tunnel inside your phone, with no server and no Internet permission. Blocking applies on metered networks; on unmetered Wi-Fi traffic passes. Stop protection any time from its switch or the notification.
Why does the app ask for no Internet permission?
Because every measurement happens on the device: Mizan reads Android\'s own counters and sends nothing anywhere, so it needs no Internet permission at all.
Why is my figure lower than the operator\'s?

The difference may be traffic from devices connected to your hotspot (not counted here yet), traffic Android\'s counters do not expose, or the operator\'s own billing method. Mizan shows what the system recorded, not an estimate.
\u201c\u2014\u201d means the value is unknown right now, not zero. It appears, for example, before Usage Access is granted or when a counter cannot be read.
How do I check the accuracy?
Compare today\'s total with the system network settings for the same window. A day monitored from midnight is more accurate than one that started mid-day, which is why partial days are labelled.
A data meter that runs on your device: it measures usage, shows speed, and warns you before a limit is crossed — no account and no Internet.
Your data stays on your device
Mizan has no Internet permission at all, and keeps every measurement and limit in a local database.
A persistent notification with speed and today\u2019s usage, plus budget alerts. You can continue without it, but alerts will not appear.
Mizan reads the network counters while it runs, and keeps going after you close the app through a permanent foreground service.
You can later block specific apps from the network from the Guard tab, after granting VPN consent in the system dialog. Nothing starts automatically.
You can change all of these options later inside the app.
